I don't really give a shit. It's awesome because small superficial things don't bother me. It sucks because I know I should be concerned or happy about some things but I just can't bring myself to care.

I like that I'm creative and can be a fast thinker. I hate that I can't do it all the time. Or at least just more often. I wish I could write a lot more and come up with more ideas for stories but sometimes there's just nothing there in my head. It's worse when someone I really like asks me to come up with something and I just draw a blank. I'm like I know this. This is what I do. Why the fuck can't I do it? Depending on the situation I can end up feeling pretty bad about drawing a mental blank like that.

Writer's block is one of the most frustrating things ever. But just like muscles you can exercise them for sustained activity. On the days you're drawing blank go find a writing prompt (there are tons of sites for this on the web including Voat and reddit) and exercise. It will turn out to be shit, I guarantee it but if you do it often enough you'll be surprised by how much you'll evolve.

You'll probably want to throw most of you prompt stories away but when the time comes and you're working on a bigger project (a novel or something for a friend or whatever) you'll find that creative block is not that bad anymore, and that at least you can produce something that can be reviewed/rewritten later on if it's not up to par.

I guess it's important to take time off too, if you try to write absolutely every single day of the year you'll burn out.

But trust me on the exercises thing: think of people like Stephen King who can publish 3 or 4 books PER YEAR! As a writer I know he has as much creative block as you and I do - the difference is that he is not an amateur but a professional and he has trained himself to just plow through it whenever it happens!
